title: Two ways in
alt: One building cut through from one street to the other, on one ground line. On the left, a person walks from the public street through the public door straight into the public program, where people sit at tables; a red fire and security wall with no door separates it from the data centre. On the right, a person walks in from the other street past bollards; a sliding gate in the fence opens for them and closes behind; at security check-in a guard behind a window checks their ID and their badge opens the door to the lobby; a glass tube lets them through alone after a badge and a biometric check; in the data hall they pass shared cabinets, locked cabinets, a mesh cage and a high-security suite with solid walls and its own door. Numbers on the drawing match a key below it.
sources: Security layers (security lobby, check-in with photo ID, mantrap entry, then colocation spaces): Equinix, 5 layers of security at Equinix IBX data centers (operator claim)
Four layers from perimeter to server room, with a revolving door or interlocking portal at each: Boon Edam, 5 Tips for Securing Data Centers (maker claim)
Glass tube that lets one person through at a time: Boon Edam Circlelock Solo product page (maker claim)
Cabinets, mesh cages and hard-walled suites: Equinix blog (2013), Cologix VAN2 and CoreSite suite pages (operator claims)
Shared cabinets (a few rack units in a cabinet shared with other clients): Supermicro glossary, What is colocation? (maker claim)
Shared rackspace offered in Vancouver: Data Center Map listing for Cologix VAN5 at 555 W Hastings (industry directory, operator-supplied)
drawn_generically: every barrier and enclosure is a generic shape; checks named are typical (badge, guard, biometric), not a specific site's
the building is drawn with a street at each end so both ways in show in one section
camera: the whole building, then the public side, then along the secure route step by step

steps.caption: One building with two ways in. On the left, the public door. On the right, from the other street, the data centre’s way in, one barrier after another.
The public door leads straight into the public program. A fire and security wall with no door separates it from the data centre.
From the street, bollards stop vehicles. The sliding gate opens only for someone expected, then closes behind them.
At security check-in a guard checks the visitor’s ID through the window, and their badge opens the door to the lobby.
The glass tube lets one person through at a time, after a badge and a biometric check.
In the data hall, clients’ equipment sits in shared cabinets, locked cabinets, mesh cages, or a high-security suite with solid walls and its own door.
